developmental_goal: Build neck, shoulder and upper-body strength needed for rolling, sitting and crawling
required_materials: Clean blanket or mat on a firm floor
activity_description: While the baby is awake and an adult is watching, lay them on their stomach on a flat, firm surface. Start with one to two minutes a few times a day and lengthen sessions as the baby grows stronger. Get down at eye level, talk, or place a toy just in front of them to encourage lifting the head. Always place the baby on their back to sleep.
cultural_relevance: Can be done on a kanga or leso spread on the floor at home, so no special equipment is needed.

activity_name: Talking and Singing to the Baby During Pregnancy
developmental_goal: Begin early familiarity with the caregivers' voices and the rhythm of home language
activity_description: From around the second trimester, the parent and other family members talk, read aloud or sing to the baby in the womb for a few minutes each day. Use a calm voice and repeat the same songs or rhymes so the sounds become familiar. This also helps parents begin bonding before birth.
cultural_relevance: Encourages singing lullabies and songs in Kiswahili, English or the family's mother tongue, and involving partners and grandparents.

developmental_goal: Support social turn-taking, shared joy, and an early understanding that people still exist when hidden
required_materials: Light cloth, or the caregiver's hands
activity_description: Face the baby, cover your face with your hands or a light cloth, then uncover it while saying 'peekaboo' with a smile. Pause to let the baby react, and repeat. As the baby gets older, let them pull the cloth away or hide their own face.
cultural_relevance: A kanga or small cloth already found in most homes works well, and the game can be played in any language.

developmental_goal: Grow receptive and expressive vocabulary by linking words to real objects
required_materials: Common household items such as a cup, spoon, ball or shoe
activity_description: During daily routines, point to an object the child is looking at and name it clearly, for example 'cup' while at mealtime. Repeat the word several times, wait for the child to look, point or try the word, and respond warmly to any attempt. Gradually add simple describing words such as 'big cup' or 'red ball'.
cultural_relevance: Uses items already in the home and supports naming in both the home language and English or Kiswahili.

developmental_goal: Develop problem-solving, cause-and-effect understanding and hand-eye coordination
required_materials: Wooden or plastic blocks, or clean empty boxes or tins
activity_description: Sit with the child and show how to stack two or three blocks, then invite them to try. Celebrate when the tower stands, and let them knock it down to see what happens. Increase the number of blocks as their skill improves, and talk about 'up', 'down', 'on top' and 'fall'.
cultural_relevance: Clean empty tins, small boxes or cut wooden offcuts are affordable substitutes for store-bought blocks.

developmental_goal: Build sensory processing and fine motor exploration through touch
required_materials: Safe objects with different textures, such as a soft cloth, a wooden spoon, a smooth gourd, or a clean sisal item
activity_description: Place a few safe, clean objects with different textures within the baby's reach while they sit or lie on their tummy. Let them touch, hold and explore each item, and describe it: 'soft', 'rough', 'smooth'. Stay close by and check that every item is too large to be swallowed.
cultural_relevance: Uses natural, locally available materials like gourds, woven sisal and cotton fabric instead of bought toys.

developmental_goal: Develop classification, comparison and early mathematical thinking
required_materials: Bottle tops, large beans or blocks in several colours and sizes; two or three containers
activity_description: Start by asking the child to put all the items of one colour into a single container. When they manage this, try sorting by size, such as big and small. Name the colours and sizes as they work, and let them check and correct their own groups.
cultural_relevance: Bottle tops, large dried beans and small baskets are low-cost, familiar materials in Kenyan homes. Supervise closely with small items.

developmental_goal: Strengthen gross motor skills, balance and coordination, and the ability to imitate and follow simple instructions
required_materials: Open, safe space indoors or outdoors
activity_description: The adult leads a simple movement, like walking on tiptoe, marching, jumping with both feet or stretching arms up high, and the child copies it. Take turns so the child also gets to be the leader. Keep moves short and fun, and add music or clapping for rhythm.
cultural_relevance: Can be played outdoors in a compound or with siblings and neighbours, and paired with familiar action songs.

developmental_goal: Support early sensory bonding through touch and voice
activity_description: Caregivers are encouraged to gently massage the belly and speak softly during pregnancy, as touch and sound can be felt by the developing baby in later stages.
cultural_relevance: No materials or cost required

developmental_goal: Build early emotional connection and turn-taking
activity_description: Hold the baby close, make eye contact, and respond to their coos and sounds with matching sounds and facial expressions, pausing to let them 'reply.'
cultural_relevance: Requires no materials; adaptable to any caregiver-child pair

developmental_goal: Support sensory regulation through calming movement
activity_description: Hold and gently rock the baby in a slow, rhythmic motion, particularly when they appear overstimulated or fussy, to help them settle.
cultural_relevance: No materials needed; can be done seated or standing

developmental_goal: Encourage early self-recognition and visual tracking
activity_description: Hold a baby-safe mirror in front of the child and narrate what they see, encouraging them to look, smile, and reach toward their reflection.
cultural_relevance: Low-cost mirrors are widely available; substitutable with any reflective safe surface

developmental_goal: Support auditory development through varied sounds
required_materials: Household items that make different sounds (e.g., rattle, crinkly paper)
activity_description: Introduce a few household items that produce different sounds and gently shake or crinkle them near the baby, pausing to watch their reaction and encourage turning toward the sound.
cultural_relevance: Uses inexpensive or repurposed household items

developmental_goal: Build emotional awareness and social imitation
activity_description: Make simple facial expressions such as smiling, surprise, or puckering lips, and encourage the child to copy them back, responding warmly to their attempts.
cultural_relevance: Requires no materials; adaptable to any family setting

developmental_goal: Develop gross motor coordination and spatial awareness
activity_description: Arrange cushions or soft household items into a simple path and encourage the child to crawl over and around them under close supervision.
cultural_relevance: Uses household items already present in most homes

developmental_goal: Build early emotional vocabulary
activity_description: During daily routines, name the child's apparent emotions out loud (e.g., 'you seem happy,' 'that felt frustrating') to help them begin associating words with feelings.
cultural_relevance: No materials required; adaptable to any language spoken at home

developmental_goal: Support sensory exploration through pouring and texture
required_materials: Shallow basin of water and safe containers
activity_description: Under close supervision, allow the child to pour water between safe containers in a shallow basin, exploring texture, sound, and cause-and-effect.
cultural_relevance: Uses water and reusable household containers

developmental_goal: Build early cooperation and patience
activity_description: Roll a ball back and forth with the child, narrating 'your turn' and 'my turn' to introduce the concept of taking turns during play.
cultural_relevance: Uses any available soft ball or toy

developmental_goal: Develop problem-solving and shape recognition
required_materials: Shape sorter or household containers with cut openings
activity_description: Provide a shape sorter, or a household container with holes cut for different shapes, and guide the child in matching shapes to the correct opening.
cultural_relevance: Can substitute purchased shape sorters with a safely modified household container

developmental_goal: Support sensory exploration through the natural environment
activity_description: Take the child on a short walk outdoors, pausing to let them touch leaves, listen to sounds, and observe things like insects or clouds, naming what they notice together.
cultural_relevance: Requires no materials or cost; adaptable to any outdoor environment

developmental_goal: Build narrative and sequencing skills
activity_description: After reading a short, familiar story together, ask the child to retell it in their own words using the pictures as prompts, offering gentle guidance as needed.
cultural_relevance: Adaptable to any locally available picture book or oral story

developmental_goal: Build responsibility and a sense of contribution
required_materials: Everyday household items appropriate for the task
activity_description: Invite the child to help with a simple, safe household task such as putting toys away or wiping a table, praising their effort and participation.
cultural_relevance: Uses only items already present in the home

developmental_goal: Support early sound recognition and vocal play
activity_description: Make simple animal sounds (e.g., 'moo,' 'woof') near the baby in an animated voice, pausing to see if they respond with their own vocal sounds.
cultural_relevance: Requires no materials; sounds can be adapted to locally familiar animals

developmental_goal: Develop balance and confidence in walking
activity_description: Hold the child's hands and encourage them to walk along a line taped on the floor or a low, stable wooden plank, supporting balance as needed.
cultural_relevance: Requires only open space; no materials needed

developmental_goal: Develop arm and leg coordination through reaching movements
activity_description: Lay the baby on a blanket with a few soft, safe toys nearby and encourage them to reach for, kick at, and bat the toys with their hands and feet.
cultural_relevance: Requires only soft toys already common in most households

developmental_goal: Develop visual tracking and attention
activity_description: Lay the baby on their back and slowly move a bright-colored toy left to right and up and down at a comfortable distance, watching to see if the baby's eyes follow its movement.
cultural_relevance: Any brightly colored household object can substitute for a purchased toy

developmental_goal: Encourage rolling and reaching to build gross motor skills
activity_description: Place the baby on their tummy or back with a toy just out of reach, and gently encourage them to roll over or stretch to reach it, celebrating when they succeed.
cultural_relevance: Uses any toy or safe household object already available

developmental_goal: Build understanding that objects still exist when hidden
required_materials: A light cloth or small blanket
activity_description: Cover your head or a favorite toy with a light cloth and see if the baby pulls it away to find what is hidden underneath, repeating the game with excitement each time.
cultural_relevance: Uses a simple cloth found in any home

developmental_goal: Support early problem-solving and cause-and-effect understanding
required_materials: A small container and a few blocks or safe objects
activity_description: Sit with the child and take turns dumping blocks or safe small objects out of a container and putting them back in, narrating the action as you play together.
cultural_relevance: Uses any small household container and safe objects

developmental_goal: Build early conversational turn-taking
activity_description: When the baby makes a sound, copy it back to them and pause to let them respond, building a simple back-and-forth exchange similar to conversation.
cultural_relevance: Requires no materials; adaptable to any language the caregiver speaks

developmental_goal: Build vocabulary through shared picture naming
activity_description: Look at a picture book or magazine together and name the objects you see as you point to them, pausing to let the child attempt the word before you repeat it clearly.
cultural_relevance: Adaptable to any locally available picture book or printed material

developmental_goal: Build balance and gross motor confidence
required_materials: A low, stable piece of furniture such as a couch or step
activity_description: Under close supervision, allow the child to practice climbing on and off a low, stable piece of furniture, staying close to offer support as needed.
cultural_relevance: Uses furniture already present in the home

developmental_goal: Build receptive language and instruction-following
activity_description: Give the child a simple one-step instruction without gestures, such as 'give me the toy,' and respond warmly when they follow it, gradually trying different simple requests.
cultural_relevance: Requires no special materials; adaptable to any home routine

developmental_goal: Develop gross motor skills through ball play
activity_description: Give the child a soft ball to kick, roll, and throw back and forth, encouraging them to try each movement in a safe open space.
cultural_relevance: Uses any soft ball available locally

developmental_goal: Support cause-and-effect understanding and fine motor problem-solving
required_materials: A toy with switches, knobs, or buttons
activity_description: Provide a safe toy with buttons, switches, or knobs and let the child explore pressing and turning them to see what happens, offering help only when needed.
cultural_relevance: Can substitute a purchased toy with a safe household item that has simple buttons or dials

developmental_goal: Build receptive language for multi-step instructions
activity_description: Give the child a simple two-step instruction, such as 'pick up the toy and put it in the basket,' offering gentle guidance the first few times before letting them try independently.
cultural_relevance: Requires no materials; adaptable to any home routine or language

developmental_goal: Build phonological awareness through rhyme and song
activity_description: Teach the child simple, familiar songs or rhymes appropriate to your language and culture, encouraging them to join in with words or actions as they learn them.
cultural_relevance: Adaptable to any local songs, rhymes, or lullabies the family already knows

developmental_goal: Build problem-solving and shape/color recognition
required_materials: A simple puzzle with shapes, colors, or animals
activity_description: Work through a simple puzzle together, naming each piece's shape, color, or animal as the child places it, offering help only when they get stuck.
cultural_relevance: Can substitute a purchased puzzle with a simple homemade shape-matching activity

developmental_goal: Build early bonding and the habit of noticing and answering the baby's signals
activity_description: When you feel the baby move or kick, pause and respond warmly: rest a hand on the spot, speak gently, and notice whether the baby moves again. A partner or another close adult can join in by feeling for movements and responding the same way, so both caregivers practise reading the baby's signals before birth.
cultural_relevance: No materials or cost; any trusted adult caregiver can take part, not only a partner

developmental_goal: Offer calm, regular sound experiences before birth
activity_description: Set aside a quiet time each day to hum or sing softly, or to listen to gentle, melodic songs while you rest. Choose music that feels calming to you and keep the sound soft.
cultural_relevance: Uses lullabies or songs from the family's own language and tradition; no cost

developmental_goal: Let the baby become familiar with the voices of the people around them
activity_description: Invite the baby's father and other close family members to take turns talking, reading or singing to the baby during pregnancy, for example in the evening when people are at home. Speak softly about what is happening that day, and pause to notice any movement in reply.
cultural_relevance: Works in whichever language the family speaks; relatives other than the father can take part

activity_name: Sharing Hopes and Worries About the Baby
developmental_goal: Support the caregiver's emotional wellbeing, which shapes the baby's early environment
activity_description: Take a few quiet minutes to think about how you feel about the baby's arrival, both the joys and the worries, and talk them over with someone you trust, such as your partner, a relative, a friend or your health worker at an antenatal visit. Talking it through can also help your family work out how they can support you. If worries feel heavy or do not ease, tell a health worker.
cultural_relevance: No cost; the trusted person can be a partner, relative, friend or health worker, depending on who is available

developmental_goal: Support the caregiver's rest and calm, which affect the baby's wellbeing
activity_description: Build a short, regular relaxing routine into the day, such as a cup of tea, a chat with a friend or an easy walk, and ask family members to take on some household tasks so you can rest. Notice what helps you feel calm and keep doing it through the pregnancy. If you are unsure how much activity suits you, check with your health worker.
cultural_relevance: Uses everyday low-cost ways to relax; family members can share household tasks

activity_name: End-of-Day Talk as a Couple or Family
developmental_goal: Build supportive communication within the family around the baby's arrival
activity_description: At the end of the day, spend a few minutes together talking about how the day went and planning for the next one, including how you will prepare for and care for the baby. Save any difficult conversations for a time when nobody is tired.
cultural_relevance: Can involve a partner or another close relative, depending on who shares the household; no cost

developmental_goal: Build a sense of safety and attachment through touch and closeness
activity_description: Hold the baby against your bare chest, with a light cover over you both if it is cool, so they can hear your voice and heartbeat and smell your scent. Keep the baby's face uncovered, and hold and comfort them often, especially when they are unsettled.
cultural_relevance: No materials or cost; can be done at home

developmental_goal: Build bonding and body awareness through playful touch
activity_description: While the baby lies on their tummy or back, run your fingers lightly along their back or tickle their hands and feet softly, smiling and talking as you play. Stop if the baby turns away or seems unsettled.
cultural_relevance: No materials or cost

developmental_goal: Help the baby feel secure and begin to recognise their own name
activity_description: Use the baby's name often when you talk to them, keeping your voice calm and gentle and smiling warmly. Sing softly, and avoid sudden loud sounds, which can upset babies.
cultural_relevance: Use the baby's name in the family's home language; no cost

developmental_goal: Build confidence and trust through shared delight and cooperation
required_materials: Safe household objects, such as a box or container
activity_description: As the baby plays, say out loud what they are doing, for example that they are putting the blocks in, and show how pleased you are with their efforts. When they struggle, offer to do it together so they feel supported while still trying for themselves.
cultural_relevance: Uses ordinary household containers; any caregiver can join in

developmental_goal: Strengthen the caregiver-child bond through regular, enjoyable shared time
activity_description: Set aside a regular time each day, ideally about half an hour, to do something together that makes the child happy, such as playing, singing, or laughing together while looking into their eyes.
cultural_relevance: No cost; any caregiver can take a turn

developmental_goal: Build a sense of belonging through shared family songs, riddles and stories
activity_description: Share songs, riddles, proverbs and stories the family already knows, in the language you speak at home, and invite grandparents, older siblings or other relatives to join in. Let the child join in with actions or dancing.
cultural_relevance: Uses songs, riddles and stories the family already knows, in its own language; extended family members can take part

developmental_goal: Teach positive behaviour by modelling it rather than punishing mistakes
activity_description: When you want the child to do something, such as sharing, waiting or speaking kindly, show them how by doing it yourself and describing what you are doing. Praise them when they copy you, and when they get it wrong, show them the better way instead of punishing the mistake.
cultural_relevance: No cost; fits into any daily routine

developmental_goal: Build conversation skills by giving the baby time to respond
activity_description: When you talk to the baby, pause and give them time to react before you speak again; silently counting to ten can help. If they do not respond, show them an example of a response, then try again with simpler words.
cultural_relevance: Works in any language spoken at home; no cost

developmental_goal: Build early language exposure and connection through face-to-face talk in the home language
activity_description: Hold the baby so you can look into their eyes, and talk to them in your home language about what you are doing or seeing. Pause to let them answer with sounds or movements.
cultural_relevance: Encourages talking in the family's own home language; no cost

developmental_goal: Introduce early counting through everyday objects
activity_description: As you go about the day, ask how many of something you can both see, such as spoons, shoes or pieces of fruit, and count them together out loud. Repeat these counting games often, because repetition helps early number skills.
cultural_relevance: Uses objects found in any home; can be done in any language

activity_name: Washing Hands and Fresh Produce Before Meals
developmental_goal: Protect the growing baby from food-borne infections
activity_description: Wash your hands with soap before preparing or eating food. Wash fruit and vegetables well in clean water before you cut or eat them. Keep raw meat away from food that will not be cooked.
cultural_relevance: Sukuma wiki, tomatoes and fruit from the market should be washed well before use.

activity_name: Cooking Meat and Eggs All the Way Through
developmental_goal: Protect the growing baby from harmful germs in undercooked food
activity_description: Cook meat, chicken, fish and eggs until they are hot all the way through, with no pink meat or runny egg. Eat food soon after cooking rather than leaving it standing for hours.
cultural_relevance: Nyama choma and fried eggs should be well done during pregnancy.

activity_name: Cutting Down on Tea and Coffee
developmental_goal: Keep caffeine within safe limits during pregnancy
activity_description: Keep caffeine to less than 200 mg a day, which is about two cups of instant coffee. Remember that strong tea, cola and energy drinks contain caffeine too. Swap some cups for water, milk or caffeine-free drinks.
cultural_relevance: Chai is part of daily life; a weaker cup or fewer cups keeps caffeine down.

developmental_goal: Plan meals with plenty of vegetables and fruit for the growing baby
activity_description: Before you go to the market or shop, write a list that includes vegetables and fruit of several colours. Planning meals and snacks ahead makes healthy choices easier when you are tired or hungry.
cultural_relevance: Mango, pawpaw, carrots, terere and managu add many colours at low cost.

activity_name: Keeping Away from Household Chemical Fumes
developmental_goal: Protect the growing baby from harmful chemicals at home and work
activity_description: Avoid breathing strong fumes from pesticides, paints and cleaning products. Open windows, wear gloves, or ask someone else to do these jobs. Ask about safety if your work involves chemicals or metals.
cultural_relevance: Ask a family member to handle insecticide sprays and paraffin while you are pregnant.

activity_name: Checking Your Vaccinations at the Clinic
developmental_goal: Protect mother and baby from serious infections through vaccination
activity_description: Ask your health worker which vaccinations you need during pregnancy and bring your clinic card. Vaccines protect you from diseases that can cause serious problems for you and your baby.
cultural_relevance: Bring your Mother and Child Health booklet so vaccines are recorded.

developmental_goal: Lower the risk of infections that can harm the growing baby
activity_description: Wash your hands often with soap and water. Keep away from people who are sick, and try not to share cups, spoons or food with young children, who often carry germs.
cultural_relevance: Keep your own cup at home so sharing with little ones is easy to avoid.

developmental_goal: Protect the growing baby from medicines and drugs that could harm them
activity_description: Do not take medicines prescribed for someone else or drugs that were not prescribed for you. Tell your health worker about every medicine you take, including ones bought over the counter, and ask which ones are safe.
cultural_relevance: Ask before taking herbal remedies or medicines from a chemist.

activity_name: Older Children Say Hello to the Bump
developmental_goal: Help the family start talking to the baby before birth
activity_description: Invite older brothers and sisters to say good morning and good night to the baby in the bump. Let them tell the baby about their day or sing a short song. Families can talk to children from birth and even before.
cultural_relevance: Siblings can greet the baby in the family's home language.

activity_name: Father's Daily Words to the Baby
developmental_goal: Help the father begin communicating with the baby before birth
activity_description: Encourage the father to spend a few minutes each day talking or singing to the baby in the bump. Fathers who communicate early enjoy being involved from the very beginning.
cultural_relevance: A father can share a family story or proverb with the baby each evening.

activity_name: Talking About Your Chores to the Baby
developmental_goal: Build the habit of talking to the baby throughout the day
activity_description: While you cook, wash or walk, describe what you are doing out loud to the baby. This builds a habit of everyday talk that you can carry on once the baby is born.
cultural_relevance: Describe cooking ugali or fetching water in your own words and language.

developmental_goal: Help the wider family share stories and voices with the baby before birth
activity_description: Ask grandparents or other relatives to tell a short story or sing a song to the baby in the bump. Families can begin talking to children even before birth.
cultural_relevance: Grandparents can pass on traditional stories, songs and riddles.

developmental_goal: Reach the weekly activity goal in short sessions
activity_description: Fit several 10-minute walks or activity sessions into your day, such as after meals or during breaks. Short sessions add up towards 150 minutes of moderate activity each week.
cultural_relevance: A short walk after lunch or to the shops counts.

developmental_goal: Stay active and flexible with gentle yoga during pregnancy
activity_description: Try gentle yoga movements suited to pregnancy, moving slowly and stopping if anything hurts. Check with your health worker first, especially if you are new to exercise.
cultural_relevance: A kanga or folded blanket works as a mat.

developmental_goal: Stay active in water, which supports the body's weight
activity_description: If you can reach a safe pool, try water aerobics or gentle swimming. Water supports your weight and can make movement more comfortable as the bump grows. Ask your health worker first.
cultural_relevance: Some hotels and community pools offer access at set times.

activity_name: Exercising Without Lying Flat on Your Back
developmental_goal: Keep exercise safe after the first trimester
activity_description: After the first three months, avoid exercises that have you lying flat on your back. Choose movements done standing, sitting or lying on your side instead.
cultural_relevance: Floor stretches can be done on your side with a pillow for support.

activity_name: Asking Others to Carry Heavy Loads
developmental_goal: Avoid heavy lifting and exhausting work during pregnancy
activity_description: Avoid lifting heavy loads such as full water containers, sacks or firewood. Ask family members to help, and rest when you feel tired.
cultural_relevance: Ask others to carry jerricans of water or bags of maize flour.

activity_name: A Walk During Your Lunch Break
developmental_goal: Build activity into the working day
activity_description: Take a walk outside during your lunch break or after work. Finding ways to be active at home and at work makes it easier to keep going.
cultural_relevance: A walk to buy lunch or around the estate counts.

developmental_goal: Ease stress during pregnancy with slow breathing
activity_description: Sit comfortably, breathe in slowly through your nose and out slowly through your mouth. Repeat for a few minutes when you feel worried or tense.
cultural_relevance: A quiet corner of the house or a bench outside works well.

activity_name: An Early Night for Enough Rest
developmental_goal: Get enough rest to manage stress during pregnancy
activity_description: Plan to go to bed a little earlier, and rest during the day when you can. Getting enough rest helps you manage stress and feel well.
cultural_relevance: Share evening chores so you can get to bed earlier.

developmental_goal: Protect mother and baby from secondhand smoke
activity_description: Move away from people who are smoking and ask your partner and visitors not to smoke near you. Secondhand smoke harms both you and your baby.
cultural_relevance: Ask smokers to step well outside the house and away from the door.

developmental_goal: Notice what causes stress and plan ways to reduce it
activity_description: Write down the things that cause you stress, then choose one or two small changes, such as resting more, exercising or talking to someone. Find a support person or group if you need one.
cultural_relevance: Women's groups and chamas can be a source of support.

developmental_goal: Stay active and connected by exercising with a friend
activity_description: Choose a friend or relative to walk or exercise with at set times. Exercise is easier and more enjoyable with company, and it lifts your mood.
cultural_relevance: Walk with a neighbour to the market or church.

developmental_goal: Gather family health information to share with the health worker
activity_description: Ask parents, grandparents and other relatives about health problems in the family, and write down what you learn. Share it with your health worker so they know what to watch for.
cultural_relevance: Family gatherings are a good time to ask older relatives.

activity_name: Writing Questions for Your Clinic Visit
developmental_goal: Feel prepared and confident at antenatal visits
activity_description: Keep a list of questions as they come to you and take it to your next clinic visit. Writing them down helps you remember what you wanted to ask.
cultural_relevance: Keep the list inside your clinic booklet.

activity_name: Planning How the Father Will Be Involved
developmental_goal: Help the father plan to take part in caring for the baby
activity_description: Talk together about how the father will hold, talk to and care for the baby from the first days. Fathers who are involved from the beginning build a strong bond with their child.
cultural_relevance: Agree on small daily tasks, such as bathing or rocking the baby.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise following movement with their eyes
activity_description: Put a puppet or sock on your hand and move it slowly up and down while saying the baby's name. Once they follow it, try moving it in a circle or other new paths.
cultural_relevance: An old sock with eyes drawn on makes a puppet.

developmental_goal: Help the baby focus on and follow an interesting object
activity_description: When the baby is calm and alert, hold a soft toy with a face within reach. Move it slowly up, down, left and right so they follow it, and let them feel how soft it is.
cultural_relevance: A homemade cloth doll works well.

developmental_goal: Help the baby focus attention and follow movement
activity_description: Do something silly in front of the baby, such as dancing or acting out an animal with its sounds. Watch them follow your movements and smile.
cultural_relevance: Act out animals the baby will meet, such as a cow or a cockerel.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise tracking a face
activity_description: When the baby is calm and alert, put your face about 20 to 25 cm from theirs and talk. Move slowly from side to side to see if they follow you. You can also try this with a toy.
cultural_relevance: Any caregiver, including siblings, can play this.

developmental_goal: Help the baby see and follow bold colours
required_materials: Toy or card in black, red and white
activity_description: Hold a toy or card with bold black, red and white patterns in front of the baby and move it slowly from side to side. Watch their eyes follow it, and perhaps their head turn too.
cultural_relevance: Draw bold patterns on card with a marker.

developmental_goal: Give the baby chances to see, hear and move freely
activity_description: Keep the baby's face uncovered while awake so they can see the world, and avoid binding them tightly for long periods. Babies need to see, hear and move their arms and legs to learn.
cultural_relevance: If you carry the baby on your back, leave their face free to look around.

developmental_goal: Help the baby tune in to the sounds of speech
activity_description: Talk to the baby slowly in a higher, sing-song voice. Babies enjoy their parents' voices, and they may try to copy your mouth and tongue movements.
cultural_relevance: Use your home language; babies enjoy any language spoken lovingly.

developmental_goal: Help the baby enjoy language through songs and actions
activity_description: Sing songs that have hand movements, such as 'Wheels on the Bus', and do the actions for the baby. Watch for smiles and movements in response.
cultural_relevance: Use Kiswahili action songs like 'Kichwa, Mabega, Magoti'.

developmental_goal: Encourage the baby to make sounds and lip movements
activity_description: Before dressing the baby, press your lips to their tummy and blow to make a funny noise. The sound and feeling make them smile and encourage them to make noises of their own.
cultural_relevance: A fun moment during dressing or after a bath.

developmental_goal: Help the baby control their tongue, ready for sounds
activity_description: Stick out your tongue slowly and wait to see if the baby copies you. Try it during nappy changes or playtime.
cultural_relevance: Older siblings enjoy playing this with the baby.

developmental_goal: Help the father communicate with the newborn
activity_description: Encourage the father to look into the baby's eyes and talk softly to them. Even a newborn sees faces and hears voices, and this is how communication begins.
cultural_relevance: Fathers can talk to the baby when they come home each day.

developmental_goal: Build strength and language through a playful carry
activity_description: Carry the baby tummy-down with one hand under their tummy. Say 'Up!' as you lift them slightly, 'Down!' as you lower them, and 'All around!' as you move side to side.
cultural_relevance: Use the words in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the baby strengthen head and neck muscles
activity_description: Hold the baby tummy-down on your chest with their head over your shoulder. Lean back slowly so they work to lift their head. Switch shoulders so both sides of the neck get practice.
cultural_relevance: Can be done while sitting on a chair or bed.

developmental_goal: Help the baby build strength in the neck, arms and tummy
activity_description: Lay the baby on their back facing you. Support behind their shoulders and head and slowly raise them to sitting, then lower them again. Once they hold their head well, practise holding their hands.
cultural_relevance: Can be done on a bed or mat.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise rolling over
activity_description: Lie next to the baby and place them on their side, supported by a rolled blanket. Talk so they reach for you until they roll. Clap when they do, then roll them back gently to try again.
cultural_relevance: A rolled kanga or shuka works as support.

developmental_goal: Help the baby develop hand-eye coordination
required_materials: String; plastic spoons or a rattle
activity_description: Hang simple safe objects, such as plastic spoons or a rattle, from a string so the baby can swipe at them. Change them every few minutes. Stay close and make sure nothing is small enough to choke on.
cultural_relevance: Use plastic measuring spoons or bottle tops on a string that are too big to swallow.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise grasping with both hands
activity_description: Move a toy or soft cloth towards the baby's hand to encourage them to grasp it. Switch sides so both hands get a turn.
cultural_relevance: A small piece of soft cloth is all you need.

developmental_goal: Help the baby move their legs and hear simple words
activity_description: With the baby on their back, gently hold their ankles and move their legs in slow circles as if riding a bicycle. Say 'go' and 'stop' as you move.
cultural_relevance: A good game during nappy changes.

developmental_goal: Help the baby feel rhythm through touch
activity_description: With the baby on their back, sing a song and gently tap the bottoms of their feet in time with the music.
cultural_relevance: Use a lullaby or children's song from your community.

developmental_goal: Help the baby become aware of their body
activity_description: Play some music and gently clap the baby's hands together. Clap in front, above their head and to each side in time with the beat.
cultural_relevance: Use songs the family enjoys.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn about their body through touch
activity_description: Gently bring the baby's hands to their face and help them stroke their cheeks. Name and touch other parts of their body as well.
cultural_relevance: Name body parts in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the baby listen and enjoy familiar tunes
required_materials: Mobile with music or a radio
activity_description: Sing along with the baby's musical mobile or with music on the radio. Hold their hand or rock them as you sing, and play the same music at other times around the house.
cultural_relevance: Radio music in the home works just as well.

developmental_goal: Give the baby new feelings to explore with their mouth
activity_description: Give the baby clean teething rings that are bumpy or smooth to explore with their mouth. This helps them use their lips, tongue and jaw.
cultural_relevance: Wash teething rings with clean water and soap.

developmental_goal: Help the baby calm and become ready to play
activity_description: Lay the baby on their back and place your hand on their chest with light, steady pressure. This can help them settle at night or become calm and alert for play.
cultural_relevance: A soothing option for any caregiver.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn early communication from expressions
activity_description: Babies watch your face closely. Show many expressions, such as happy, surprised and silly, and watch the baby respond with their own.
cultural_relevance: Any family member can join in.

developmental_goal: Help the baby become calm and alert so they enjoy play
activity_description: Hold the baby close, about 20 to 25 cm from your face, and smile. Change the tone of your voice to get their attention. When they are calm and looking at you, it is time to play.
cultural_relevance: A good moment after a feed or nap.

developmental_goal: Help the father bond with the newborn through touch
activity_description: Encourage the father to hold the baby closely and gently stroke their skin. Soothing an upset baby also helps them learn to calm themselves.
cultural_relevance: Fathers can take over cuddling while the mother rests.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn that someone will respond to their needs
activity_description: Respond to the baby's cries, sounds and movements as soon as you can. Babies learn to trust that someone will pay attention to them, which builds a secure bond.
cultural_relevance: Everyone who cares for the baby can respond in the same caring way.

developmental_goal: Support the caregiver's well-being so they can care for the baby
activity_description: Caring for a new baby is hard work. Rest when you can, eat well and ask family or friends for help. Looking after yourself helps you care for your baby.
cultural_relevance: Ask relatives or neighbours to help with meals or chores.

activity_name: On and Off with Lights and Taps
developmental_goal: Help the baby notice cause and effect
activity_description: Show the baby how lights, taps and the radio turn on and off, saying 'On!' and 'Off!' each time. A torch beam moving around the room is fun to watch too.
cultural_relevance: A torch or phone light works where there is no mains power.

developmental_goal: Help the baby watch and follow movement
activity_description: Show the baby a toy that moves or pops up, such as a wind-up toy. Let them watch it move again and again, and see their surprise.
cultural_relevance: A spinning top or a rolling bottle top can work too.

developmental_goal: Help the baby focus their eyes and explore a face
activity_description: Make different faces at the baby: smile, frown or stick out your tongue. Let them touch your face and explore your nose, mouth and other features.
cultural_relevance: Grandparents and siblings can take turns making faces.

developmental_goal: Help the baby focus attention while following your movements
activity_description: When the baby plays with their feet, touch each toe and say a number for it, or sing 'This Little Piggy'. Watch them follow your hands.
cultural_relevance: Count toes in Kiswahili: moja, mbili, tatu.

activity_name: What Could It Be? Soft Toy Game
developmental_goal: Help the baby explore an object by looking and touching
activity_description: Show the baby a favourite soft toy and help them touch it. Ask what it could be, then tell them: 'It's a kitty!'
cultural_relevance: Use a homemade cloth animal.

developmental_goal: Help the baby listen to and compare sounds
activity_description: Use household items such as newspaper or a squeeze toy to make noises. Repeat sounds softly and a little louder (never too loud) and in different orders. Then help the baby make the sounds.
cultural_relevance: Crumpled paper and a plastic bottle make good sounds.

developmental_goal: Help the baby enjoy your voice and pictures in books
activity_description: Read to the baby in different places, such as outside or during tummy time. Reading can simply mean describing the pictures without following the words.
cultural_relevance: Describe pictures in any book or magazine at home.

developmental_goal: Help the baby build body awareness and early language through rhymes
activity_description: Wiggle the baby's fingers and toes as you sing a counting rhyme, or clap their hands together while you repeat a clapping rhyme. Repeating rhymes builds early language.
cultural_relevance: Use clapping rhymes from your own childhood.

developmental_goal: Expose the baby to new sounds through simple stories
activity_description: Make the baby's toys come to life by acting out simple stories with them. Give each toy its own voice and sounds.
cultural_relevance: Tell a short traditional story using toys or household objects.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn words for actions
required_materials: Doors, cupboards or containers with lids
activity_description: Say 'open' and 'close' as you use doors, cupboards and containers with lids. Make up a little song as you go: 'Open and close it, clap, clap, clap'.
cultural_relevance: Use a sufuria lid or a cupboard door.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn to get your attention with sounds and gestures
activity_description: During calm moments, walk slowly past the baby. When they try to get your attention with sounds or movements, stop, smile and talk to them.
cultural_relevance: Any familiar caregiver can play.

developmental_goal: Help the baby connect words to pictures
activity_description: Look at a picture book together and point to the objects, animals and plants on each page while you name them.
cultural_relevance: Name animals the baby may see locally, such as goats and chickens.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise reaching and strengthen the core
activity_description: Place toys in front of the baby during tummy time to encourage reaching. Try to get them to use both arms, then move the toy from side to side for more challenge.
cultural_relevance: Use any safe household object as a toy.

developmental_goal: Help the baby shift their weight and balance while sitting
activity_description: While the baby sits with support, place toys slightly out of reach so they shift their weight to get them.
cultural_relevance: Prop the baby with cushions on a mat.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn the movement of rolling over
activity_description: If the baby can't yet roll over alone, hold one leg and slowly guide them through rolling onto their tummy. Practise rolling to both sides.
cultural_relevance: Use a mat or blanket on the floor.

developmental_goal: Help the baby build strength while exploring their feet
activity_description: Draw the baby's attention to their feet. If they need help, give a small lift under their hips. Let them do as much as they can on their own.
cultural_relevance: A playful moment during nappy changes.

developmental_goal: Help the baby work on hand-eye coordination and core strength
activity_description: Gently place a soft ring toy around the baby's foot and lift the foot into view. Encourage them to reach for it.
cultural_relevance: A soft hair band or cloth ring works too.

developmental_goal: Help the baby build head control and enjoy movement
activity_description: Once the baby can hold their head up, lay them tummy-down on a blanket. Hold the corners and slowly pull them around a clear, safe room.
cultural_relevance: A shuka or thick kanga works well on a smooth floor.

developmental_goal: Expose the baby to new sounds outdoors
activity_description: Go for a walk and let the baby hear the sounds around them. Talk about what you hear: 'Do you hear the birds singing? The wind is moving the leaves.'
cultural_relevance: Point out matatu horns, birds and children playing.

developmental_goal: Give the baby new sensory experiences while you cook
activity_description: Keep the baby safely near you while you cook, well away from heat. Let them smell the foods and talk about what you are doing.
cultural_relevance: Let them smell onions, dhania or ripe mangoes.

developmental_goal: Give the baby new types of movement
activity_description: Sit the baby upright on your lap and gently move your knees up and down, then side to side. Hold on to them firmly.
cultural_relevance: Sing a song while you ride.

developmental_goal: Help the baby develop a sense of balance and body position
activity_description: Carry the baby securely in a carrier or wrap while you sweep or tidy. Talk about what you see and do as you move around the house.
cultural_relevance: Carrying the baby in a kanga on your back is a common way to do this.

developmental_goal: Help the baby explore textures and movement
activity_description: Hand the baby a ball with different textures and see what they do. Show them how to roll it or drop it into a box.
cultural_relevance: A ball made from tied cloth or a soft sponge works too.

activity_name: A Chewing Toy for Sore Gums
developmental_goal: Help the baby soothe themselves while teething
activity_description: When the baby cries from teething, offer a clean toy or cloth made for chewing.
cultural_relevance: Wash teething items well with soap and clean water.

developmental_goal: Make tummy time playful and build connection
activity_description: While the baby is on their tummy, cover your face with your hands. When you reappear, say their name with a big smile.
cultural_relevance: Older siblings can lie down and play too.

developmental_goal: Help the baby connect while practising sitting
activity_description: Sit the baby on your lap facing you, lightly supporting their trunk. Smile and talk to them, and offer a toy to see if they reach for it.
cultural_relevance: A good time for talk in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the baby feel loved and secure
activity_description: Give the baby lots of loving attention and cuddles. Praise them warmly when they smile, coo or try something new.
cultural_relevance: Every family member can show warmth and praise.

activity_name: Noticing When Baby Needs a Break
developmental_goal: Help the caregiver respond to the baby's signals during play
activity_description: Play with the baby when they are alert and relaxed. If they turn away, fuss or look tired, stop and let them rest before playing again.
cultural_relevance: Watching the baby's signals helps any carer.

activity_name: A Change of Scene to Calm
developmental_goal: Help a fussy baby become calm and alert
activity_description: If the baby is fussy or stressed, change their surroundings: move to a quieter room, step outside or dim the light. This can help them reach a calm, alert state.
cultural_relevance: A short walk outside in a carrier often helps.

developmental_goal: Help the baby solve a simple problem with their fingers
activity_description: Wrap a familiar toy loosely in newspaper and let the baby unwrap it. Clap when they get it open and name what is inside.
cultural_relevance: Old newspaper is perfect for wrapping.

developmental_goal: Help the baby remember and find a hidden sound
activity_description: Help the baby squeeze a squeaky toy to hear the sound. Then cover it with a blanket and squeak it again. Help them pull off the blanket to find it.
cultural_relevance: A crackly bottle under a cloth works too.

developmental_goal: Help the baby follow movement with their eyes
activity_description: Use your hands to make shadow puppets on the wall. Talk and sing as you move your fingers while the baby watches.
cultural_relevance: Use a torch or a lamp in the evening.

activity_name: Many Ways to Use a Toy
developmental_goal: Help the baby learn by watching how you play
activity_description: Show the baby different ways to use toys, such as banging blocks together or knocking over a small tower. Then let them try.
cultural_relevance: Wooden off-cuts or empty boxes work as blocks.

developmental_goal: Help the baby watch how things move
required_materials: Plastic bottle; beads or rice; strong glue
activity_description: Put beads or rice in a small plastic bottle and glue the lid on firmly. Let the baby shake it and watch the contents move. Check the lid often.
cultural_relevance: Use a small water bottle and dry beans or rice.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn to focus their attention
activity_description: As you do chores, point to objects and say what you are doing. Help the baby point with their finger and give them something safe to hold, like a wet cloth.
cultural_relevance: Let them 'help' wipe a low table.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise back-and-forth communication
activity_description: Ask the baby questions and wait for their sounds or babbles in reply. Record the conversation and play it back for them to hear.
cultural_relevance: Share the recording with relatives far away.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn words for parts of the face
activity_description: Point to parts of your face and name them: 'Mummy's nose.' Then point to the same parts on the baby's face and watch how they react.
cultural_relevance: Name face parts in your home language too.

developmental_goal: Help the baby develop listening and talking skills
activity_description: Talk into a pretend phone as if you are making a real call, then offer it to the baby to have a turn.
cultural_relevance: An old switched-off phone is a favourite toy.

developmental_goal: Help the baby attach words to shapes, sizes and textures
activity_description: Name the shape, size and feel of things the baby plays with: 'Look at this big red ball', 'This teddy is so soft.'
cultural_relevance: Describe fruit at the market: a big round orange.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn names of body parts
activity_description: Ask the baby where their feet are. When they point, say 'Hello, feet!' Keep going with other body parts.
cultural_relevance: Play in Kiswahili: 'Miguu iko wapi?'

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn to follow simple directions
activity_description: Give a simple instruction like 'Roll the ball' or 'Clap your hands'. Show them how, then smile and clap when they do it.
cultural_relevance: Use simple requests in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the baby build upper body strength while crawling
activity_description: Lie on the floor and call the baby by name to crawl over you. Hug them when they reach you. Add another person for extra crawling.
cultural_relevance: Siblings love being part of the obstacle.

developmental_goal: Help the baby coordinate movements to reach toys around them
activity_description: Place toys in a large circle on the floor and lay the baby tummy-down in the middle. Watch them reach and move around to play.
cultural_relevance: Use safe household items in the circle.

developmental_goal: Help the baby balance and strengthen the core while sitting
activity_description: With the baby sitting, place toys in front of them, then slowly move them to the side so the baby reaches across their body.
cultural_relevance: Use spoons or cups as toys.

developmental_goal: Help the baby strengthen legs and practise standing
activity_description: While the baby stands holding a low surface, put toys lower down or on the floor so they squat to reach and stand back up. Celebrate each time they come up.
cultural_relevance: A low stool or bench works well.

developmental_goal: Help the baby practise climbing and changing position
activity_description: Set up a small, sturdy chair nearby. Use your voice or a toy to encourage the baby to climb into it. Let them play kneeling or turn and sit.
cultural_relevance: A small wooden stool works well.

developmental_goal: Help the baby build strength through crawling and listening
activity_description: Roll a soft ball across the room and say 'Ready, set, go!' so the baby crawls after it.
cultural_relevance: A ball made of rolled cloth or paper works.

developmental_goal: Expose the baby to new sights, smells and sounds outdoors
activity_description: Take the baby outside and let them touch leaves and grass safely. Talk about what they touch, smell, see and hear: 'The rock feels hard.'
cultural_relevance: Explore the shamba or compound together.

developmental_goal: Help the baby use their senses during water play
required_materials: Plastic container with a lid; nail to punch holes
activity_description: Punch small holes in the lid of an empty plastic container. Fill it with water at bath time so the baby can make it 'rain' on themselves or a toy.
cultural_relevance: An empty yoghurt tub works well.

developmental_goal: Soothe the baby's gums when teething
required_materials: Clean washcloth; freezer or cold water
activity_description: Put a clean wet washcloth in the freezer for about 15 minutes, or soak it in cold water. Give it to the baby to bite on before it gets hard.
cultural_relevance: Cold clean water works if there is no freezer.

developmental_goal: Give the baby new kinds of movement
activity_description: Sit the baby on your knees, hold their hips and move your legs up and down like a horse. Change the way they face so they can look at you or at the room.
cultural_relevance: Add a traditional riding song.

developmental_goal: Help the baby develop core strength and balance
required_materials: Beach ball or large soft ball
activity_description: Blow up a beach ball so it is a little soft. Hold the baby carefully tummy-down on top and roll them slowly back and forth and side to side.
cultural_relevance: Hold the baby firmly the whole time.

developmental_goal: Help the baby develop movement and sensory skills
activity_description: If the baby can sit up and hold up their head well, place them securely in a baby swing and push gently back and forth.
cultural_relevance: Many public parks have baby swings.

developmental_goal: Help the baby feel heard by copying their actions
activity_description: Watch what the baby does and copy them. If they bang a block or clap, do the same. Let them lead the play.
cultural_relevance: Siblings can join in copying.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn to express pleasure with movement
activity_description: Clap with excitement when the baby does something good and encourage them to clap with you.
cultural_relevance: The whole family can cheer together.

developmental_goal: Help the baby explore with confidence
activity_description: Let the baby explore your home on their own while you stay close by to keep them safe. Remove dangers at their level.
cultural_relevance: Keep sharp items and charcoal stoves out of reach.

developmental_goal: Help the baby learn to copy and take turns
activity_description: Sit on the floor facing a bucket. Drop a toy in, then let the baby have a turn.
cultural_relevance: Use a small basin and a bottle top too big to swallow.

developmental_goal: Help the baby feel capable by helping with a simple task
activity_description: Ask the baby to pick up scattered toys and bring them to you. Thank them warmly when they do.
cultural_relevance: Make tidying a cheerful family routine.

developmental_goal: Help the child notice similarities and differences
activity_description: Gather two or three kinds of objects, such as cups, socks and spoons. Show the child how to put the same things together, then let them try. Ask them to hand you a certain object: 'Can you give me the spoon?'
cultural_relevance: Use everyday kitchen and laundry items.

developmental_goal: Help the child begin pretend play by copying adults
required_materials: Old handbag; old phone; keys; photos
activity_description: Fill an old bag with safe items like the ones you carry, such as an old phone, keys and family photos. Watch the child take them out and play with them just like you.
cultural_relevance: An old kiondo or handbag makes a great play bag.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore everyday objects safely
required_materials: Low cupboard; wooden spoons; plastic cups
activity_description: Keep one low cupboard open while you are in the kitchen and fill it with safe items such as wooden spoons, plastic cups and bowls for the child to explore.
cultural_relevance: Plastic cups and a mwiko (wooden spoon) are favourites.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise matching and sorting
activity_description: Play simple matching games, such as putting shapes into a sorter or fitting large puzzle pieces. Help at first, then let them try on their own.
cultural_relevance: A box with cut-out holes makes a homemade shape sorter.

developmental_goal: Help the child build memory and anticipation
activity_description: Hide yourself under a blanket and let the child pull it off for the big reveal. Take turns hiding.
cultural_relevance: A shuka or kanga works well.

developmental_goal: Help the child use imagination in play
activity_description: Join in pretend play, such as rocking a teddy to sleep or singing into a wooden spoon as a microphone. Take turns so the child copies and leads.
cultural_relevance: A cooking stick makes a good pretend microphone.

developmental_goal: Help the child build vocabulary through rhythm and rhyme
activity_description: Listen and sing along to children's songs with simple rhythms and rhyming words, at home or while travelling.
cultural_relevance: Sing on matatu or bus journeys.

developmental_goal: Help the child understand simple instructions
activity_description: Speak to the child simply using real words rather than baby talk. Give short directions like 'Roll the ball' and show them what you mean.
cultural_relevance: Use clear words in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn colour words through water play
required_materials: Wide shallow container; water; flowers or leaves
activity_description: Float flowers in a shallow container of water. Point to each one and say its colour, then ask the child to point to and pick up a flower.
cultural_relevance: Bougainvillea and other garden flowers work well.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn the words in and out
activity_description: Ask the child to put objects into a box or bucket and take them out again. Say 'in' and 'out' each time.
cultural_relevance: A basket and some clothes pegs work well.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn that pointing has meaning
activity_description: When the child points, name what they point to and ask a question: 'Would you like that toy?' Wait for their answer.
cultural_relevance: Ask in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the child listen and follow song directions
activity_description: Sing songs with instructions, like the Hokey Pokey, and dance together, following the directions.
cultural_relevance: Use Kiswahili action songs that name body parts.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise walking while carrying things
activity_description: As the child walks more confidently, ask them to carry light objects from one place to another.
cultural_relevance: Let them carry a plastic cup or small basket.

developmental_goal: Help the child balance without holding on
activity_description: Offer the child a toy to hold while they are standing so they practise balancing without using their hands.
cultural_relevance: Stay close for safety.

developmental_goal: Help the child build balance and kicking skills
activity_description: Encourage the child to kick a ball on the ground. Once they are steady, gently roll the ball towards them to kick.
cultural_relevance: A ball made from plastic bags and string works well.

developmental_goal: Help the child improve balance while dressing
activity_description: While the child stands holding your shoulders, encourage them to lift one foot and put it into the trouser leg.
cultural_relevance: Part of the morning routine.

developmental_goal: Help the child coordinate movement and balance
activity_description: Blow up a balloon and let the child chase it around the room. They may catch it if you toss it gently. Always stay with them in case it pops, and throw away burst pieces.
cultural_relevance: Balloons from celebrations can be reused.

developmental_goal: Help the child use their fingers to build fine motor skills
required_materials: Old sock with the toe cut off; balls
activity_description: Cut the toe off an old sock and show the child how to push balls or plastic eggs through it.
cultural_relevance: Use balls of rolled paper too big to swallow.

developmental_goal: Help the child develop touch and coordination
activity_description: Take the child to a sandpit or beach with a small spade and bucket and let them dig and pour.
cultural_relevance: A heap of clean building sand at home works too.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore how paint feels
activity_description: Cover the table with newspaper and pour paint onto a plate. Help the child press their hand in the paint and then on paper. Talk about how it feels, and keep paint out of their mouth.
cultural_relevance: Display the handprints on the wall.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore touch safely
activity_description: Let the child draw with plain yoghurt on a paper plate instead of paint. It is safe if fingers go in their mouth.
cultural_relevance: Use a little mala or yoghurt.

developmental_goal: Help the child strengthen their hands through water play
activity_description: Add sponges of different shapes and colours to bath time. Let the child squeeze and soak them.
cultural_relevance: Cut a kitchen sponge into shapes.

developmental_goal: Help the child develop their sense of balance
activity_description: Lie on your back with knees bent and shins level. Place the child tummy-down on your shins, hold them firmly and gently rock side to side or bounce up and down.
cultural_relevance: Hold on to the child the whole time.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn how textures feel
activity_description: Read books with different textures and let the child touch them. Use words for what they feel: rough, bumpy, soft.
cultural_relevance: Glue pieces of fabric into a homemade book.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn to interact through music
activity_description: Tap a simple rhythm on a cardboard box with a wooden spoon and let the child copy you. Take turns leading.
cultural_relevance: An upturned sufuria makes a drum.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn play and copying skills
activity_description: Act silly like a clown: pretend to fall down, walk funny and jump around. Encourage the child to copy you.
cultural_relevance: Siblings make great clowns.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise copying and enjoy playing together
activity_description: Put funny hats on yourselves and look in the mirror together. Do a little dance and talk about what you are wearing.
cultural_relevance: Use caps, scarves or a kofia.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise caring play and fine motor skills
activity_description: During play, encourage the child to feed their soft toys with a baby spoon.
cultural_relevance: Use a plastic plate and spoon from the kitchen.

developmental_goal: Help the child build independence
activity_description: Let the child help pull on clothes and feed themselves, even if it is slow and messy. Praise their effort.
cultural_relevance: Allow extra time in the morning routine.

developmental_goal: Help the child put parts together into a whole
activity_description: Cut a picture the child likes into a few large pieces and help them put it back together.
cultural_relevance: Use a picture from a calendar or magazine.

developmental_goal: Help the child notice what is different
activity_description: Put out a group of similar items and one that is different, such as green blocks and one red block. Ask the child which one is not like the others.
cultural_relevance: Use maize cobs and one potato, or similar.

developmental_goal: Help the child search using spoken clues
activity_description: Hide an item and let the child search. Say 'warmer' as they get closer and 'colder' as they move away. Show them how the game works at first.
cultural_relevance: Play inside the house or compound.

developmental_goal: Help the child build problem-solving and memory
activity_description: Hide the child's favourite toys around the house and give clues to help them find them.
cultural_relevance: Hide toys under cushions or behind doors.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn how things move down a slope
required_materials: Board or tray; balls or bottles
activity_description: Make a ramp with a board or tray and let the child roll different objects down it. Talk about which go fast and which go slow.
cultural_relevance: A piece of wood propped on a step works.

developmental_goal: Help the child remember colours and directions
activity_description: Draw squares of different colours with chalk outside. Ask the child to walk to a colour: 'Go to the red square.' Then try two colours in a row.
cultural_relevance: Use coloured chalk on a cemented area.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise saying new words
activity_description: Say a new word and let the child try to repeat it. Clap, cheer and say the word back each time they try.
cultural_relevance: Try words in Kiswahili and your home language.

developmental_goal: Bring stories to life to build language and attention
activity_description: Add sound effects as you read. If someone stomps in the story, stamp your feet. If a dog barks, bark!
cultural_relevance: Use animal sounds in traditional stories.

developmental_goal: Help the child follow simple requests
activity_description: While you fold laundry, ask the child to bring you different items: 'Please bring me a sock.'
cultural_relevance: Fold clothes together after washing day.

developmental_goal: Help the child tell stories with shadows
activity_description: Turn off the lights and shine a torch. Show the child how to make shadows with hands or body, and tell a story together using them.
cultural_relevance: Good for evenings when the power is off.

developmental_goal: Help the child understand place words like under and behind
activity_description: Place bright objects around the room and tell the child where to look: 'Look under the table.'
cultural_relevance: Use bottle tops or fruit.

developmental_goal: Help the child use imagination and sounds
activity_description: Put the child in a large box and pretend it is a car. Make engine noises and turn a pretend steering wheel together.
cultural_relevance: Pretend to drive a matatu with stops and fares.

developmental_goal: Help the child build movement and follow directions
activity_description: Dance together. When the music stops, freeze; when it starts, dance again.
cultural_relevance: Use popular local music.

developmental_goal: Help the child build balance and problem-solving
activity_description: Challenge the child to cross the room on a path of pillows, picking up the one behind and putting it in front.
cultural_relevance: Cushions from the sofa work.

developmental_goal: Help the child build balance and hand-eye coordination
activity_description: Put an egg on a spoon and ask the child to walk a short distance without dropping it. Use a real egg outside.
cultural_relevance: A potato on a spoon works too.

developmental_goal: Help the child build hand-eye coordination
activity_description: Stand up empty bottles as pins and show the child how to roll a ball to knock them down.
cultural_relevance: Reuse empty water bottles.

developmental_goal: Help the child build pinch and finger control
activity_description: Stick tape or stickers on a table and let the child peel them off with thumb and finger. Lift an edge to help them start.
cultural_relevance: Masking tape is cheap and easy to peel.

developmental_goal: Help the child build fine motor skills by threading
activity_description: Let the child thread large pasta tubes on to string to make a necklace. They can paint the pasta first.
cultural_relevance: Use macaroni or large beads.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore cold and watch colours spread
required_materials: Ice tray; food colouring; basin of water
activity_description: Freeze water with food colouring in an ice tray. Let the child drop the cubes into a basin of water and watch them melt and spread colour.
cultural_relevance: Plain ice works too if there is no colouring.

developmental_goal: Help the child find objects by touch
activity_description: Hide a toy in a bucket of sand and let the child search for it. For a challenge, ask them to find it with their eyes closed.
cultural_relevance: Use clean sand in a basin.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore how paint feels under their feet
activity_description: Let the child step in paint and walk on paper to make a picture. Do this outside or on a plastic sheet.
cultural_relevance: A good outdoor activity on a sunny day.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore colour and touch without mess
activity_description: Put some paint in a sealed zip bag and tape it shut. Let the child squish and poke the bag to move the paint around.
cultural_relevance: Use a strong plastic bag tied tight.

developmental_goal: Help the child build finger skills and enjoy sounds
activity_description: Let the child pop bubble wrap. Encourage them to use just their thumb and index finger.
cultural_relevance: Save bubble wrap from deliveries.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore sounds with their fingers
activity_description: Stretch rubber bands of different sizes around a thin box. Let the child strum them with one finger to hear the different sounds.
cultural_relevance: A shoebox works well.

developmental_goal: Help the child build social and imaginative play
activity_description: Set up a pretend tea party with the child's soft toys. Ask them questions about their toys and encourage them to talk to them.
cultural_relevance: Serve pretend chai and mandazi.

developmental_goal: Help the child feel included in family tasks
activity_description: Let the child help you in the kitchen by stirring and mixing ingredients. Guide their hands if needed.
cultural_relevance: Let them stir porridge flour and water before cooking.

developmental_goal: Help the child play outside and meet other children
activity_description: Take the child to a playground to explore, swing and slide. They get to play near other children too.
cultural_relevance: Visit a local park or school playground.

developmental_goal: Help the child enjoy a joyful chasing game
activity_description: Chase the child around saying 'I'm going to get you!' and let the excitement build before you catch them for a hug.
cultural_relevance: Siblings love joining in.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore roles through dress-up
activity_description: Fill a box with old clothes, hats and fabric. Let the child dress up and step into different characters.
cultural_relevance: Use old kitenge, scarves and hats.

developmental_goal: Help the child think ahead and explain ideas while reading
activity_description: While reading, ask what is happening in the pictures and what might happen next. Ask for a little more detail in their answers.
cultural_relevance: Use local storybooks or family stories.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore cause and effect and solve problems
activity_description: Offer toys where pressing a button or pulling a lever makes something happen. Let the child work out how they work.
cultural_relevance: A torch with a switch or a radio knob is fascinating.

developmental_goal: Help the child compare sizes using simple questions
activity_description: Ask simple questions and listen to the answers: 'Which ball is bigger?' 'Where is your brother?' Questions like these get children thinking and talking.
cultural_relevance: Compare fruits, cups or shoes at home.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore interests and use objects creatively
activity_description: Give the child time for free play where they choose what to do and use objects in new ways. Stay close but let them lead.
cultural_relevance: Boxes, bottle tops and cloth make endless play.

developmental_goal: Help the child make patterns and pictures with natural objects
activity_description: Make simple pictures or patterns together by arranging pebbles, shells or seeds. Display the finished creation.
cultural_relevance: Use beans, maize seeds or stones from the yard.

developmental_goal: Help the child start pretend play
activity_description: Let the child dress up in adult clothes like shoes, hats and shirts and pretend to be a grown-up.
cultural_relevance: Let them pretend to be a teacher, doctor or shopkeeper.

developmental_goal: Help the child fill in words in a familiar song
activity_description: Sing simple songs that name body parts, then pause to see if the child fills in the word or touches the body part.
cultural_relevance: Sing 'Kichwa, Mabega, Magoti na Vidole'.

activity_name: Naming Clothes and Colours While Dressing
developmental_goal: Help the child learn words during the dressing routine
activity_description: As you dress the child, name each piece of clothing and its colour: 'Here's your blue shirt.'
cultural_relevance: Use colour words in Kiswahili and English.

developmental_goal: Help the child talk more by responding to their questions
activity_description: Encourage the child to talk, and answer their questions patiently. Listening and responding shows them their words matter.
cultural_relevance: Older relatives can answer questions too.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn stories, songs and games
activity_description: Teach the child a short story, song or game and repeat it often until they can join in.
cultural_relevance: Pass on traditional stories and songs.

activity_name: Talking About What You See on the Bus
developmental_goal: Help the child learn new words on outings
activity_description: On walks or bus rides, point out and name what you see, and ask the child what they notice.
cultural_relevance: Talk about matatus, shops and animals on the way.

activity_name: Would You Like the Red Cup?
developmental_goal: Help the child answer simple choice questions
activity_description: Offer simple choices with questions like 'Would you like the red cup?' and wait for their answer.
cultural_relevance: Use any everyday choice.

developmental_goal: Help the child build coordination by carrying light items
activity_description: Let the child help set the table by carrying light things like cups or napkins. Thank them for helping.
cultural_relevance: Plastic cups are safest.

developmental_goal: Help the child build hand skills in the kitchen
activity_description: Give the child simple kitchen jobs, such as washing vegetables in a basin or stirring a mixture.
cultural_relevance: Washing sukuma or tomatoes is a good first job.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise pulling and turning
activity_description: Let the child help open drawers and doors, such as when putting clothes away or going outside.
cultural_relevance: Keep fingers clear of hinges.

activity_name: Turning Pages One at a Time
developmental_goal: Help the child build finger control
activity_description: Show the child how to turn the pages of a book or magazine one at a time.
cultural_relevance: Old magazines are fine for practice.

developmental_goal: Help the child build drawing skills outside
activity_description: Let the child draw with chalk on a pavement or cemented area. Build up to drawing lines and circles.
cultural_relevance: Use school chalk on a veranda.

activity_name: Drawing with a Stick in the Sand
developmental_goal: Help the child practise drawing with simple tools
required_materials: Stick; patch of sand or soil
activity_description: Give the child a stick to draw lines and shapes in sand or soil, or let them use chalk on a board.
cultural_relevance: A patch of sand in the compound works well.

developmental_goal: Help the child get used to new tastes
activity_description: Offer small tastes of new foods alongside foods they know. Try again later if they refuse.
cultural_relevance: Try local foods like arrow roots, pumpkin or managu.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore water and lead the play
activity_description: At bath time, let the child lead the play with cups and containers. Join in with what they choose to do.
cultural_relevance: A basin bath with a cup works well.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore textures, shapes and sounds
activity_description: Give the child safe kitchen items to explore and describe them together: smooth, heavy, noisy.
cultural_relevance: Use sufuria lids, wooden spoons and plastic bowls.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore outdoors in their own way
activity_description: Spend time outdoors and follow the child's lead in choosing how to play.
cultural_relevance: Explore the compound, shamba or local park.

developmental_goal: Help the child wind down for sleep
activity_description: Keep a calm, regular bedtime routine, such as a wash, a quiet song and a story. Children this age need 11 to 14 hours of sleep a day, including naps.
cultural_relevance: A soft lullaby in your home language helps.

developmental_goal: Help the child feel proud of their work
activity_description: Do simple art together and put the child's work on the wall for the family to see.
cultural_relevance: Stick drawings on the wall of the sitting room.

developmental_goal: Help the child learn that tantrums do not win attention
activity_description: Give less attention to tantrums and more to calm, positive behaviour. Stay calm and nearby until the child settles.
cultural_relevance: All carers can respond the same way.

developmental_goal: Help the child show upset in respectful ways
activity_description: Teach the child respectful ways to show they are upset, such as saying 'I'm angry' instead of hitting.
cultural_relevance: Use simple feeling words in your home language.

developmental_goal: Help the child feel good about following instructions
activity_description: When the child follows an instruction, praise them right away: 'Thank you for putting your shoes away.'
cultural_relevance: Praise in front of family members too.

developmental_goal: Help the child feel independent by making choices
required_materials: Two snacks or two sets of clothes
activity_description: Offer the child two healthy options for a snack or clothes and let them choose.
cultural_relevance: Offer a banana or an orange.

developmental_goal: Help the child practise taking turns
activity_description: Take turns building a tower of blocks together, then let the child knock it down.
cultural_relevance: Use wooden off-cuts or empty boxes.
